title: Tagged invoice & chargeback templates — UX notes
content:
Context:
This is a working note for the console UX around tagged invoices and automated chargeback templates. Goal: make it frictionless for finance and platform teams to export invoice artifacts that include tag-level breakdowns, templates for chargebacks, and automated attachment generation for monthly bill distribution.

Why this is important:
- Customers (platform teams / FinOps) frequently ask for per-team and per-project tags on invoices to run internal chargebacks.
- Current export only supports flat CSV and does not surface tag inheritance rules. This increases manual work and errors.
- We want to reduce manual steps and support a repeatable template system for invoice emails that attached a) full invoice PDF b) tag-level CSV and c) reconciliations summary.

High-level requirements (working):
- UI to define an "Invoice Template" that controls: cover email subject/body, which CSV attachments (full vs tag-split), tag precedence rules, and optional rounding rules for cents.
- Per-organization default template and ability to override per-billing-account.
- Export flow should support: manual export, scheduled monthly dispatch, and on-demand chargeback run (one-click split + download).
- CSV schema must include: invoice_id, period_start, period_end, account_id, tag_kv pairs (tag keys standardized), token_cost_usd, storage_cost_usd, network_cost_usd, discount_usd, allocation_basis (token/usage/flat), allocation_percent, allocated_amount_usd.
- Preserve mapping to original usage lines for audit (line_id reference).

Wireframe / flow sketches (notes for product mock):
1) Billing > Exports > New Template modal:
   - Fields: Template name, default recipients (comma-separated), include_pdf (checkbox), include_tagged_csv (checkbox), tag-selection (multi-select), tag-fallback order (drag to reorder), rounding policy (round up/nearest/none), preview examples (sample CSV row).
   - CTA: Save Template; secondary: Run Preview (generates sample file using last closed month).

2) Invoice list > Invoice actions > Apply Template / Export with Template:
   - Apply Template opens a quick confirmation with recipients and attachments toggles.
   - For scheduled templates show schedule pane with cron-like quick presets (monthly EOM, 1st of month) and timezone setting.

3) Chargeback run flow (first-run wizard):
   - Step 1: Select invoice(s) or month range
   - Step 2: Choose template or create new
   - Step 3: Review allocation preview table (top 20 tags shown, ability to search tags)
   - Step 4: Confirm & dispatch — shows estimated runtime and link to background job status.

Edge cases / friction points to handle:
- Missing tags (unassigned usage): add a "Unallocated" bucket and option to distribute proportionally vs assign to default team tag.
- Dynamic tags where key names vary across accounts (e.g., "team" vs "team_name"): provide a small mapping UI to rename keys before export and a detection step during preview.
- Very high cardinality tags causing huge CSVs: add limit warnings and an option to group by first n tags or sample aggregated rolls for top N.
- Discounts & credits: should be allocated proportionally unless explicit rule applied in template.
- Rounding drift: allow customers to choose a rounding policy and show how residual cents are allocated (e.g., highest remainder to carrier).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Product: Template create/edit/delete flows in Console; templates persisted per-org; templates selectable at export time.
- Export: CSV export contains tag columns as selected; includes line_id reference for audit.
- Scheduling: Basic monthly schedule with timezone and recipients; scheduled job appears in Jobs table with status and downloadable artifacts.
- Preview: Run Preview returns a sample CSV and highlights missing tags and key mapping suggestions.
- Audit: Each scheduled dispatch creates an audit event with template id, triggering user, and attachment links.

Backlog / follow-ups (priority-ish):
- [P0] CSV schema verification with Finance (Sofia) — ensure allocation math aligns with existing accounting processes (Jira BILL-1982).
- [P1] Add templating variables for email body ({{org_name}}, {{period_end}}, {{total_due}}).
- [P1] S3/GCS export targets for scheduled jobs (customers want direct bucket pushes).
- [P2] Chargeback preview UI performance tuning for invoices > 1M lines (streaming preview).
- [P2] Option to export per-account PDFs (split one invoice into N PDFs by tag).

Open questions / requires decisions:
- How do we represent multi-dimensional tags (e.g., team + environment + project)? Flatten? Provide nested grouping? (ask accounting)
- Should scheduled exports be free for all plans or limited to Enterprise / Dedicated customers?
- Do we surface template sharing across orgs or keep org-private?

Design notes / microcopy ideas:
- "Include tagged breakdown CSV" tooltip: "CSV lists cost by tag key/value pairs and includes a pointer to original usage lines for auditing."
- Preview empty state: show sample rows + callout: "We detected missing tags on ~12% of usage. Consider adding a fallback rule to avoid unallocated charges."
- Error state when export job fails: show retriable action "Re-run with new template" and link to logs.

Implementation hints for engineering (from preliminary infra sync):
- Reuse existing exports job framework; add a transform stage that reads usage lines and applies tag precedence rules before emitting CSV rows.
- Store template as small JSON blob in billing DB (name, tag_order, recipients, attachments, schedule). Keep schema stable; add version field for migrations.
- For scheduled pushes to buckets, implement signed-url write with retries; preserve object metadata with invoice_id and template_id.

Notes from meeting 2024-11-07 (raw):
- Ravi: need to keep line_id so finance can reconcile down to token-level.
- Noah: customers asked for ability to attach a short reconciliation note per tag — maybe a freeform column in CSV for admin notes.
- Maya: we should prototype UI in Figma quickly and ship preview first to get early feedback.

Next steps (owners):
- Maya: create initial Figma frames for modal + preview (due 2024-11-21).
- Sofia: confirm allocation math and CSV columns with accounting (due 2024-11-14).
- Eng (Ravi): spike transform stage to emit sample CSV from last closed month (due 2024-11-30).

Quick links / refs:
- Current export runbook (internal): CONFLUENCE-4021
- Customer ask thread: slack #customer-finance thread ts=1701...

This doc is a working draft — expect edits. Keep feedback inline below.
